Citizen: Stay indoors between 11:00 and 16:00 wherever possible.
Drink water at regular intervals even when not thirsty.
Wear light-coloured, loose cotton clothing and cover the head when outside.
Check on elderly neighbours, infants, and people with chronic illness.
Recognise heat exhaustion: dizziness, nausea — move to shade and seek help.
Farmer: Avoid heavy field work during peak afternoon heat.
Ensure livestock have access to shade and drinking water.
Monitor crops for heat and moisture stress.
Shift irrigation to cooler hours where possible.
Health Department: Ensure cooling centres and emergency facilities are prepared.
Increase public health messaging during peak heat.
Local Authority: Open public cooling spaces where required.
Coordinate water supply and emergency response.
